races.name: Ladies Day 9th May "Confined" Novice Stakes (No more than two runs) (GBB/GBBPlus Race) (Div I)

runners_data.name: Tripoli Flyer
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist switching from hurdles who gets the likely slow pace but needs to prove Flat ability translates
runners_data.comment: Smart bumper/novice hurdle form; well held behind Constitution Hill on Flat debut
runners_data.spotlight: Smart bumper/novice hurdle form; recorded an RPR of 141 when eighth in the County Hurdle four weeks ago; no match for Constitution Hill on his Flat debut but he should do better in this sphere at some point, probably when handicapping.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity as debut runner for powerful Michael Bell yard, breeding suggests stamina
runners_data.comment: $85,000 yearling; half-brother to two winners out of a useful dirt winner; 1m2f a query
runners_data.spotlight: $85,000 yearling; fourth foal; half-brother to winners Exude (Canadian 1m3f turf) and Investment Mandate (US 1m/8.5f turf); dam US 8.5f dirt winner (including stakes; RPR 109); stable in good form but 1m2f a query given his sire.

runners_data.name: Director's Cut
runners_data.note: Only confirmed pace-setter returning after 132 days off, likely to get uncontested lead
runners_data.comment: 1m AW win on second 2yo start; new trip should suit but he has a penalty to shoulder
runners_data.spotlight: Two runs in November, fifth on debut (8.6f) before putting that experience to good use at Newcastle 19 days later where he finished strongest to beat 11 rivals (1m); new trip should suit and he is bred to carry on improving; the penalty does ask a stiffer question though.

runners_data.name: Hatteen
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed promise second time out, this longer trip should suit
runners_data.comment: Only beat one rival in two 2yo runs but the 2nd effort was encouraging; longer trip a plus
runners_data.spotlight: Last of three on debut (1m, soft) and fifth of six on his second 2yo run (8.3f, good to soft); the latter effort wasn't without promise, however, and this longer trip should be right up his street.

runners_data.name: Infraad
runners_data.note: Highest-rated hold-up horse who will benefit from likely slow pace, 166 days off a concern
runners_data.comment: Green but made a pleasing debut at Doncaster in October (1m, soft); likely big improver
runners_data.spotlight: In need of the experience when second of five in a 1m maiden at Doncaster (soft) last October; flattered by his proximity to the idling winner but it was still an encouraging start and today's extra yardage looks a big positive; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Grazeon Sunshine
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner better suited to handicaps, outclassed at this level
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner but down the field in two Flat runs; minor handicaps beckon
runners_data.spotlight: Useful in bumpers but he has finished down the field in two Flat starts this year; handicaps likely to see him in a better light.

runners_data.name: Bay Royale
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who tired over shorter last time, extra distance appeals on paper
runners_data.comment: Promising debut here (8.3f) in October, tiring final furlong; much more to come this year
runners_data.spotlight: Got tired in the final furlong when fourth of nine in an 8.3f maiden (soft) here in October, but it was still an encouraging start to his career; the longer trip should suit and this Irish Derby entrant is open to plenty of improvement this year.

runners_data.name: You Got To My Soul
runners_data.note: Strong hold-up horse whose Southwell form has been boosted, perfect race shape
runners_data.comment: Latest Southwell 3rd is solid form; can do better & holds solid form claims on turf debut
runners_data.spotlight: Both runs at Southwell; promise on debut (1m) and better form when third over 1m3f in February, form which has been bolstered by the second and fourth since; leading form claims now switched to turf.

runners_data.name: That Darn Cantor
runners_data.note: Needs significant improvement from poor debut, hold-up style suits race flow
runners_data.comment: 40-1 when tailed off at Newmarket in October (1m, good); bred to leave that well behind
runners_data.spotlight: 40-1 and always behind in a 1m novice at Newmarket (good ground) in October on sole 2yo run; bred to leave that behind him in time.

races.paceDynamic: Director's Cut is the only confirmed front runner and will face no early pressure, allowing him to dictate a comfortable gallop through the early stages. The prominent runners Hatteen may try to sit close, but with most of the field preferring hold-up tactics (Tripoli Flyer, Infraad, Bay Royale, You Got To My Soul, That Darn Cantor), there's limited early speed. This sets up a tactical affair where the pace will likely be modest early before quickening from the 3-furlong pole. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can deliver late kicks, as they'll get the soft lead they need to unleash their finishing speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Director's Cut gets an easy lead and the hold-up horses leave their runs too late
scenarios.body: Director's Cut faces no pressure through steady fractions and has enough left to repel late challengers on this return to a longer trip. The lack of early pace plays into his hands as prominent racers often benefit when they're not bustled along early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and multiple hold-up horses produce strong finishes simultaneously
scenarios.body: The modest early gallop sets up perfectly for the closers who get the exact race shape they need to unleash their turn of foot. Infrared and You Got To My Soul have the highest ratings among the hold-up brigade and can exploit the tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Creates
scenarios.trigger: If Hatteen or another prominent runner decides to press Director's Cut early
scenarios.body: The increased pace suits the hold-up horses even more as it sets up a stronger gallop for their finishing kicks. Those on the pace get softened up while the back markers get ideal conditions to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Inexperience Costs Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Director's Cut or other prominent runners make tactical errors given their limited experience
scenarios.body: The novice nature of this field means positioning mistakes are likely from those who haven't learned racecraft yet. This opens the door for more experienced campaigners or those with stronger jockey/trainer combinations to capitalize.

watchPoints.text: Director's Cut could steal this if he gets too easy a lead and the field leaves it too late to chase
Watch for any early pressure on Director's Cut from Hatteen as it would completely change the race dynamic
Infraad has been off 166 days which is a long break for a lightly-raced three-year-old
Mr Bollinger is a complete unknown making his debut for the powerful Michael Bell stable
The modest early pace could set up too well for multiple hold-up horses creating a blanket finish

races.name: Ladies Day 9th May "Confined" Novice Stakes (No more than two runs) (GBB/GBBPlus Race) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Monte A Bord
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner who has a useful Flat pedigree and he needs watching in market on his return
runners_data.spotlight: 45,000gns yearling; close second on bumper debut at Kelso (2m, good) last September and he justified favouritism in similar conditions at Newcastle the following month; this is a different test on his return but he has useful Flat pedigree and needs watching in market.

runners_data.name: Australia Day
runners_data.comment: 180,000gns yearling; plenty to like on paper and he's an interesting newcomer
runners_data.spotlight: 60,000gns foal, 180,000gns yearling; fourth foal; gelded half-brother to winners Zenga (Listed-placed 9.4f AW; RPR 97) and Surpass (7f/7.4f 2yo; 96); dam 7f 2yo winner (85); half-sister to Group-placed 7f/1m winner Ricetta, out of half-sister to outstanding miler Kingman; plenty to like on paper and he's an interesting newcomer.

runners_data.name: Olympic Charter
runners_data.comment: Has a smart pedigree and yard is 3-7 in novice events this year; striking debutant
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth foal; closely related to 5f AW winner Nordic Games (RPR 73), half-brother to three winners including Beautiful Love (1m/1m3f including US Grade 3; 115) and Flying Honours (7f-1m2f 2yo including Group 3; 108); dam 1m1f-11.5f winner (including Group 3; 105); yard 3-7 in novice events this year and he's respected on debut.

runners_data.name: Outback Legend
runners_data.comment: 80,000euros yearling; yard is in good form and interesting to see how he figures in market
runners_data.spotlight: 80,000euros yearling; sixth foal; half-brother to winners Maksud (Listed-placed 1m2f; RPR 107), Capel At Dawn (1m; 76) and Haajoos (Spanish 8.5f-9.5f); dam 9.4f AW winner (78), half-sister to US 7f/1m Grade 1 winner Gabby's Golden Gal; yard is in good form and interesting to see how he figures in market on debut.

runners_data.name: Tornado Tower
runners_data.comment: 850,000gns yearling; has striking pedigree and he needs a close look on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 850,000gns yearling; fifth foal; brother to winners Hurricane Lane (1m-14.5f including triple Group 1; RPR 125) and Frankel's Storm (1m 2yo/1m4f; 98), half-brother to 1m4f-2m2f winner Sweet William (including Group 2; 120); dam 15.5f-2m winner (including /Listed; 103); has a striking pedigree and he needs a close look on debut.

runners_data.name: Qarreeb
runners_data.comment: Made a low-key start at Wolverhampton in November and he needs a transformation on return
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to two useful winners but he made a low-key start when seventh of ten at Wolverhampton (8.6f) in November; should know more this time but he needs a transformation upped in trip on his return.

runners_data.name: Knightsail
runners_data.comment: Some promise in his two runs last autumn and he's in the mix on his return
runners_data.spotlight: 125,000gns yearling by Camelot; beaten around 6l in his two runs in the autumn, most recently when third of seven at Goodwood (1m1f, good) in October; doesn't set a high standard on that form but this step back up in trip looks a good move and he should have more to offer this season.

runners_data.name: The Bitters
runners_data.comment: 150-1 and she finished tailed off on Newcastle debut (1m, AW) last month
runners_data.spotlight: 150-1 and she finished tailed off on Newcastle debut (1m, AW) last month.

runners_data.name: Plutarch
runners_data.comment: Tailed off in the second of his two runs at Wolverhampton in December; opposable on return
runners_data.spotlight: Out of a 7f Listed winner; shaped with some promise when a staying-on fourth on Wolverhampton debut (1m4f) in December, but he was tailed off on his return visit two weeks later; was never travelling in that race and has something to prove on his return.

races.name: Flat Is Back Restricted Novice Stakes (For horses in Bands B, C and D) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Greek Street
runners_data.comment: 52,000gns half-brother to four winners; dam a 7f 2yo winner; market revealing
runners_data.spotlight: April foal; 32,000gns foal, 52,000gns yearling; sixth foal; half-brother to winners Mister Wilson (7f 2yo/8.5f Flat, RPR 92; 2m hurdle), Pietro (6f/7f including 2yo; 91), Port Winston (5f 2yo; 73) and Hidden Pearl (1m6f; 68); dam French 7f 2yo winner; stable not known for precocious juveniles but worth a market check all the same.

runners_data.name: Blackberry Bold
runners_data.comment: £50,000 half-sister to a winner in Italy; dam a winning 2yo; yard going well; sole filly
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; £50,000 yearling; second foal; half-sister to Italian 5f/6f 2yo winner Korhogo; dam 5f/5.4f winner (including 2yo; RPR 94); stable going along nicely and their first 2yo runner of the year performed with credit at Bath on Sunday; sole filly in the field.

runners_data.name: Top Cote
runners_data.comment: 15,000euros yearling; dam a 7f 2yo winner (RPR 99); betting to guide
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; 7,000euros foal, 15,000euros yearling; first foal of a 7f 2yo winner (RPR 97), out of French 10.5f winning half-sister to 1m1f Flat and 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase winner Authentic Act; first 2yo runner of the year for the stable; betting to guide.

runners_data.name: Invincible Isaac
runners_data.comment: Lost all chance at the start in the Brocklesby but clear promise mid-race; can do better
runners_data.spotlight: 66-1 and beaten over 15l in the Brocklesby on debut, but he lost all chance when completely blowing the start; showed clear promise with that in mind and he shouldn't be underestimated here if breaking cleanly.

races.name: Four Legged Friend 26th April Handicap

runners_data.name: J Street
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has shown some form for new connections but lacks a recent win
runners_data.comment: Shaped nicely at Doncaster ten days ago; still capable of better; interesting contender
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from 12 starts but she ended her time with Ivan Furtado with a good second at Wolverhampton in October (third past the post) and both runs for her current stable have threatened better; should get a good pace to aim at here and she is an interesting contender.

runners_data.name: Bang On The Bell
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning to turf after disappointing AW winter, veteran headgear wearer
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts this winter; not a solid option now returning to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Out of sorts this winter; tumbled down the weights but not a solid option now returning to turf.

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: Prominent runner back from long 170-day break with previous turf form credentials
runners_data.comment: Three 5f wins last year; she needs to raise her game to defy this mark but it's possible
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins last season for Grace Harris; beaten but not discredited off this mark on her final three runs in 2025; got loose before the start of her intended reappearance last month (50-1 at the time); Rossa Ryan always a positive booking for the stable.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse fit from recent AW runs with strong turf record on good ground
runners_data.comment: Return to turf in his favour and he lurks on a dangerous mark; one for the shortlist
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple turf winner on good ground or slower; fit from AW, where he has run well in two of his three runs this year; should be in the thick of it.

runners_data.name: Glory Fighter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with course and distance success, 61 days since last decent third
runners_data.comment: C&D winner; close third on AW when last seen in February; high on the list
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-time turf winner, including C&D; close third at Newcastle when last seen in February; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Komorkis
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on 173-day break since moving to new trainer Mullaney from Fahey
runners_data.comment: Won a 3-runner novice for R Fahey as a 3yo; sold 1,400gns since last seen; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: 1-5 for Richard Fahey, the win coming in a three-runner novice at Newcastle last September (8-1 outsider of the three); sold for 1,400gns in October; improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Spendmore Lane
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with recent AW wins but historical starting issues, wears headgear
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back AW wins this year; slow start a hindrance in hat-trick bid latest; turf query
runners_data.spotlight: The starts have been an issue for her but she finally got her act together when winning a 5f handicap at Chelmsford in February; followed up at Wolverhampton soon afterwards but she blew the start in her hat-trick bid at Chelmsford five days later; has a bit more to prove on turf but she can't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Fiorella Princess
runners_data.note: Sole front runner under top pilot Doyle, holds tactical advantage but others have more pace
runners_data.comment: Arrives on the back of some fair AW runs; others appeal as being better treated though
runners_data.spotlight: Still 5lb higher than for her last win but she has been running with credit on AW for new trainer in recent starts; others appeal more for win purposes.

races.paceDynamic: Fiorella Princess will take the field along from the front in what should be a manageable pace over this minimum trip. The prominent runners J Street, Bang On The Bell, Over Spiced and Glory Fighter will track her without applying serious early pressure, while the hold-up horses Albegone, Komorkis and Spendmore Lane will need to be produced with well-timed runs. With only one confirmed front runner and several patient types at the back, this sets up as a tactical affair that will strongly favour the closers who can produce the strongest finish in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and the closers get clear runs
scenarios.body: The patient types will have too much finishing speed for the leaders who went too early. Spendmore Lane's recent AW form and Albegone's turf record make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Over Spiced or Glory Fighter travel perfectly and kick clear
scenarios.body: The winner will have tracked the pace without getting involved early before producing a sustained drive. Their class and experience tells in a finish where the hold-up horses don't quite get there.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Fiorella Princess gets too soft a lead and stays on strongly
scenarios.body: The pace proves too slow for the closers to make up the ground despite their finishing kick. Hollie Doyle judges it perfectly from the front and they can't peg her back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Long-Shot Success
scenarios.trigger: If Komorkis or Bang On The Bell find significant improvement
scenarios.body: The market gets it wrong as a less fancied runner produces career-best form returning to turf. They benefit from the tactical nature and slip through when others are watching the favourites.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Spendmore Lane's starting behaviour given her historical issues from the gates
Monitor how much of a lead Fiorella Princess gets early as it could determine if closers can catch her
Observe Over Spiced's fitness after 170 days off following her intended comeback mishap
Check if the hold-up horses Albegone and Komorkis get clear runs in the straight
Watch Bang On The Bell's turf return after a poor winter on artificial surfaces

races.name: Family Funday 31st May Handicap

runners_data.name: Glenna
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed her best form on soft ground as a 2yo; step up to 1m2f should suit and David Probert booking is positive despite 196-day break
runners_data.comment: Promise in three novice runs over shorter last year; new trip a plus; opening mark no gift
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in three novice runs (7f-1m; best run on soft ground) as a 2yo; bred to appreciate the extra distance but she needs to prove this opening mark is in range.

runners_data.name: Dryburgh
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who improved markedly when fitted with hood and stepped up to 1m2f at Doncaster; 10-day turnaround keeps him sharp under new trainer
runners_data.comment: Promising third at Doncaster ten days ago (hooded first time); remains capable of better
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 for Jane Chapple-Hyam; low-key stable debut in February but he took a good step forward fitted with a hood and upped to 1m2f when third at Doncaster ten days ago; travelled strongly there and he remains open to further progress; good chance.

runners_data.name: Causing Problems
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fitted with hood and tongue-tie for handicap debut; warm favourite last time suggests connections expect improvement but needs to prove it
runners_data.comment: Pulled too hard when disappointing favourite on recent h'cap debut; needs to settle better
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field in three 2yo runs; fitted with a hood for his handicap/seasonal debut at Wolverhampton nine days ago, a race where he was sent off a warm favourite but pulled his chance away early; tongue-tie now added; will need to settle better now upped in class.

runners_data.name: Extraterrestrial
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with low mileage who showed promise in handicap debut at Wolverhampton; visor fitted suggests further improvement expected
runners_data.comment: Promising 3rd on handicap debut (9.4f, AW); needs more but the new visor could prompt it
runners_data.spotlight: Promising start to his handicap career when third of five at Wolverhampton last month (9.4f, AW); he will need more to come out on top but he is low mileage and the addition of a visor can give him a lift.

runners_data.name: Port Darwin
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with proven course form; 5lb claimer reduces his burden and recent Goodwood win gives him clear fitness edge over returning rivals

runners_data.name: Femme Fatale
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 183-day break; her best 2yo form came at middle distances and this trip extension should suit perfectly
runners_data.comment: One encouraging 2yo run (1m1f, good to soft); market useful handicapping after a break
runners_data.spotlight: The second of her three 2yo runs was respectable (1m1f, good to soft) and she should have no problem with this trip and further; market to guide back from six months off.

runners_data.name: Al's River
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 153-day absence; fair autumn form but needs to prove stamina for this extended trip on breeding
runners_data.comment: Promise at 2yrs but the new trip/gelding operation not enough to tempt this time
runners_data.spotlight: Fair form in three quick runs last autumn, finishing third of 14 at Chelmsford on the most recent of them (1m); stamina in bottom half of his pedigree but this opening mark will demand improvement; gelded since last run.

runners_data.name: Tiny Riot
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose latest Southwell form has been compromised by subsequent poor runs from that race; plugged on when given time suggesting trip will help
runners_data.comment: Modest form from 6f-7f but this son of Sottsass may be a different proposition over 1m2f
runners_data.spotlight: The form of his latest seventh of eight at Southwell (7f) has taken some knocks and he was never the slightest threat in a steadily run affair; did plug on though and he could prove a different proposition now up in trip for his handicap debut; Dan Skelton still seeking a first Flat winner but that is unlikely to remain the case for long and Rossa Ryan has been booked; one to consider.

runners_data.name: Any Which Way
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with stamina concerns who faded in previous runs; 160-day break and step up in trip may help but has history of disappointing in finish
runners_data.comment: Work in progress last year; likely big improver now upped in trip and handicapping
runners_data.spotlight: Looked a work in progress in three 2yo runs, showing his best form on the second occasion (1m, good to soft); looks sure to improve for 1m2f on paper and he returns with his stable going well.

races.paceDynamic: Port Darwin will likely take this race forward with limited early competition, setting a controlled tempo from the front. Glenna and Femme Fatale may track him prominently but neither are confirmed pace-pressers. With six hold-up horses in the field including Dryburgh, Extraterrestrial and Any Which Way, there will be significant traffic behind a modest early gallop. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable squeeze and take advantage of the sustainable pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Port Darwin gets an easy lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The moderate pace will leave him with plenty in reserve while the hold-up horses get caught in traffic behind. His recent Goodwood win shows he can capitalize when getting his own way in front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Glenna or Femme Fatale sit handy and pounce late
scenarios.body: They avoid the traffic problems while staying close enough to the steady pace to strike when Port Darwin tires. The step up in trip suits both fillies' profiles perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Dryburgh's recent Doncaster third shows his closing kick when getting a true run, while Extraterrestrial's Wolverhampton form suggests untapped potential. Both need significant luck in running.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge Port Darwin for the early lead
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly strong pace would set up the race for the genuine hold-up horses, though this seems unlikely given the field composition. The lack of natural pace-pressers makes this scenario improbable.

watchPoints.text: Port Darwin must be watched for how easily he gets to the front - if unchallenged he could steal this with Jack Callan's 5lb claim
Dryburgh's market position will be crucial given his quick turnaround and recent improvement under new trainer Oli Rix
Any hold-up horse that gets prominent early positioning should be noted as most will need significant luck from off the pace
Glenna's fitness after 196 days off needs monitoring but David Probert's presence suggests she's ready to go
The pace through the first half-mile will determine everything - if slow it becomes Port Darwin's race to lose

races.name: £9 Racedays At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap

runners_data.name: Revich
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Hollie Doyle who excels on good ground and has the class edge despite 16 days absence
runners_data.comment: On a long losing run but he didn't get much luck at Wolverhampton last month; in the mix
runners_data.spotlight: All seven wins have been on good or slower ground on turf; last success was in 2023 but he didn't get much luck when fourth at Wolverhampton (7f) last month and he's in the mix on this step back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Needs the return to turf after two poor AW runs but ten-time winner who handles the distance well
runners_data.comment: Ten-time turf winner who is on a reduced mark and needs a close look back in this sphere
runners_data.spotlight: Ten-time turf winner and her last success was at Carlisle (1m, good) last August; well held in last four starts but last two have been on AW and she may have needed her reappearance run last month; now 7lb lower than for her last win and she needs a close look back in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Future Cutlet
runners_data.note: Stepping back up in trip after struggling at shorter distances but 175 days off track is concerning
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in six runs for current yard and he needs a transformation after 175 days off
runners_data.spotlight: Won in Ireland (7f) in 2024 but he was unplaced in six runs for new yard last year; mark continues to fall but he needs a transformation back up in trip after six months off.

runners_data.name: Powerful Response
runners_data.note: Prominent racer suited by recent turf form with Sam James taking over from claim rider
runners_data.comment: Dual turf winner who could be in the mix but he wouldn't want the ground to dry out
runners_data.spotlight: First win was on AW but last two have come on turf (8.3f/1m2f, soft); had some close calls on Tapeta during the winter and he was a creditable fourth in big field at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) 11 days ago; could be in the mix again but he wouldn't want the ground to dry out.

runners_data.name: Antiquity
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won on Polytrack last time and drops significantly in class from recent outings
runners_data.comment: C&D winner who has been in good form on AW this year; respected back on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Won on Polytrack at Lingfield (1m) in February and was fair fifth in a Class 5 event at Wolverhampton last month; remains feasibly treated on his best form and his five turf runs include a win over C&D (good) last April; respected on this drop back in grade.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but poor recent form suggests he's regressed from his better days

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Front runner who will contest the lead but hasn't won in 12 attempts and form is moderate
runners_data.comment: 0-12 and no better than midfield on his last four starts; others are more convincing
runners_data.spotlight: 0-12 and no better than midfield on his last four starts; dropping down the weights but his best recent effort came in cheekpieces and others are more convincing.

runners_data.name: Sir David
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 191-day break but has winning form on good ground at this trip

runners_data.name: Amber Honey
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly with visor fitted but inconsistent record suggests she's hard to trust
runners_data.comment: Dual AW winner but she didn't fire at Wolverhampton last time; bit to prove back on turf

races.paceDynamic: The Sweet Escape and Our Misty Blue are the confirmed front runners who will contest the early pace in this 15-runner handicap. With both pace-setters being relatively moderate performers, they're likely to set an honest gallop rather than a breakneck speed, especially over this staying trip of 1m½f. The large field means horses will be well spread out, creating opportunities for different tactical approaches. This pace scenario favours hold-up horses and prominent racers who can pick up the pieces when the early leaders come under pressure in the final three furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape and Our Misty Blue set a steady tempo without burning out
scenarios.body: The honest gallop allows hold-up horses to close strongly up the Nottingham hill. Patient rides on classy animals prove most effective when the early pace collapses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runners Collapse Late
scenarios.trigger: If both pace-setters fade dramatically in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Prominent racers tracking the leaders inherit the race as the field comes to them. Mid-division horses with tactical speed can surge past the tiring front rank.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Genuine End-to-End Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates a strong tempo throughout with no let-up
scenarios.body: The sustained pace finds out stamina deficiencies and rewards horses with proven staying power. Only the most genuine stayers can maintain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If neither front runner shows early speed creating a slow crawl
scenarios.body: The lack of pace turns this into a sprint finish where position and luck in running become crucial. Horses with turn of foot rather than stamina dominate the finish.

races.paceDynamic: Light The Night Up is the sole confirmed front runner and will set a measured gallop without pressure through the first half-mile. The real congestion comes behind him where five horses (Venetian Romance, Kokushoku, Aneirin's Sword, Smartanck, Gloriola) all want prominent positions, creating inevitable traffic problems turning for home. This bottleneck will favor the patient hold-up horses like Bearin Up, Kokoluna, Saint Of The Sea, Bird Of War and Crimson Rambler who can sweep around the scrimmaging pack. The race shape strongly favors hold-up horses who can stay wide and avoid the prominent traffic jam.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack bunches up badly 2f out creating a wall of horses
scenarios.body: The patient back-markers swing wide with clear runs while the prominent runners get caught in a speed-sapping traffic jam. Horses with tactical speed from off the pace capitalize on others' misfortune.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent horse gets first run before the traffic develops
scenarios.body: A single horse from the congested prominent pack manages to kick clear before the jam forms, stealing a march while others get shuffled back. The lone escapee builds an unassailable lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Light The Night Up goes too slowly and nobody wants the lead early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sitting duck scenario with a sprint from the 2f pole, turning into a pure speed test. Horses with natural finishing kick benefit from the tactical crawl.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Light The Night Up gets soft sectionals and the field goes to sleep
scenarios.body: The leader gets away with murder in front, building an insurmountable advantage while the field dawdles behind expecting others to make the running. By the time they react, it's too late.

Venetian Romance faces a fitness test on turf return but could benefit if getting an uncontested prominent pitch
Saint Of The Sea and Crimson Rambler both have tactical speed to sweep around traffic problems late

races.paceDynamic: Just An Hour will lead from flag to finish as the sole confirmed front runner, setting a sustainable gallop without pressure early. Four horses (Moon Beginnings, Monty Beau, Love Beach, Qitaal) will create congestion in the prominent positions behind the leader, causing traffic problems turning for home. The hold-up brigade (Cavolo Nero, Kind Of Kiss, Secret Beach, Jez Bomb) will face a wall of horses ahead with limited room to maneuver. This race shape strongly favours the leader Just An Hour and any prominent horse that can secure a clear run, while the hold-up horses will struggle to find racing room when it matters.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Just An Hour maintains his gallop and the prominent horses don't press him hard enough early.
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader keeps finding and holds off late challenges, while the packed prominent group gets in each other's way approaching the turn. Just An Hour's fitness edge after 166 days off becomes irrelevant when he's not being pressured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent horses create a wall behind Just An Hour with nowhere to go at the business end.
scenarios.body: Moon Beginnings or Love Beach find the gaps that others can't, benefiting from their prominent style without getting trapped. The hold-up horses are completely shut out by the traffic jam ahead of them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Find Room
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion creates enough pace to set up the race for closers with clear runs.
scenarios.body: Cavolo Nero and Jez Bomb get dream splits up the rail or around the outside as the pace collapses. Their superior recent form tells when getting the right trip they've been denied lately.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits All
scenarios.trigger: If Just An Hour goes too slow early and gets swamped by everything in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace means every horse gets their chance and it becomes a sprint from the 2f marker. Recent form and class become the deciding factors rather than racing luck.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems at the 3f pole when Moon Beginnings, Monty Beau, Love Beach and Qitaal all arrive behind Just An Hour simultaneously

Love Beach's 161-day absence could tell late despite his tactical advantage from prominent position
Watch Edward Greatrex's handling of Mighty Quiet on return - stable running at 0/4 in last 14 days needs bounce back
